title: 1812: Potawatomi lodges by the river all year
items: A small Potawatomi camp now stands on the river's south bank just west of the creek mouth on every day of 1812: two mat lodges, an elm-bark house, two fires, a drying rack and two canoes drawn up by the water.
Currey writes that families came and went all year to trade furs and camped by the river near the creek mouth. Outside the August gathering, these lodges are the camp you find there.
